one_month_reasoning: AMAT's FQ4 FY26 report is on 2026-11-12, outside the window ending 2026-10-29. Inside the window are sector read-throughs that can move semicap either way: Micron FQ4 tonight (Sep 30, after the close; it has already said every FY27 quarter's capex will be above the ~$10B FQ4 level, so a capex beat is partly expected), Samsung preliminary results (~Oct 7), ASML Q3 (Oct 14), TSMC Q3 (~Oct 15, first 2027 capex colour), Lam Research (Oct 21), Intel (~Oct 22), SK hynix and hyperscaler capex guidance (~Oct 27-29). KLA may land at or just after the window's end. The BIS Affiliates Rule suspension formally ends Nov 9 and is reportedly extended to Jan 10, 2027, so neither date falls inside the window. The stock is +23% off the $415.38 Sep-16 closing low (not ~$424 as I wrote in round 1), including +5.2% on 9/29 alone. I treat short-term reversal and momentum as roughly cancelling. In round 1 I centred slightly below spot; I now centre at spot, because the customer-capex prints have positive skew on the numbers but the positioning after the rebound is stretched. I use a symmetric lognormal with median $512 and monthly sigma 17% (60% / 3.5 ≈ 17%, left there because of the event cluster).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (Sep-2027 NTM EPS $21.5, a 10% skeptic haircut to the $23.85 FY28 consensus, x 23.5x + $8/sh net cash = $513, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (NTM net income $17.0B x 72% conversion = $12.2B at a 3.0% late-cycle yield = $516/sh, weight 0.4). The main change from round 1 is anchoring on consensus FY28 EPS; I keep the skepticism in an explicit haircut and a de-rated multiple.

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener AMAT finances page (source 18, id 4850, Applied Materials): FY27 EPS 18.43 on re-check (citation gate 2026-10-15); the gate's first-pass not_found took this page for Citigroup's, which is id 4818. Yahoo (source 8) showed $18.47, 35 analysts, range $16.02-21.77 on 2026-10-15.
MarketScreener AMAT finances page (id 4850): FY28 EPS 23.85; FY28 net sales 55,857M on re-check (citation gate 2026-10-15), +0.6% drift from $55.5B on 2026-09-29.

FY28 consensus $23.85 less a 10% haircut. Revenue growth of +20% in FY28 is above SEMI's +14.1% 2028 WFE path (source 20), and Castellano (13) sees 2027-28 digestion with AMAT share flat, so year-2 consensus at a late-cycle point is more likely to be revised down than up. The haircut is larger than the supervisor's 6% because the skeptic view is that out-year consensus is the thing that breaks first in a semicap cycle. $21.5 still implies +17% growth over FY27, consistent with SEMI's positive 2028 path.

Today the stock is ~27.7x FY27 and ~21.5x FY28 consensus ($512/$23.85). By Sep 2027 the market will be pricing FY28-29 late in the cycle, so I de-rate from 27.7x (MS Equal-weight on valuation, source 9; SA 'priced for perfection' and 'downgrade to Hold' on premium vs KLA/Lam/ASML, sources 11 and 25). I stay above AMAT's ~18x downturn multiple because of the AI and packaging mix. 23.5x is down from 25x in round 1 because it now applies to a higher EPS base, and the cycle-peak discount belongs on the multiple.

Cash + investments $14.50B less debt $6.54B (ST $1.30B incl. $1.2B 2027 notes, LT $5.25B) = $7.96B, or $10/share on 793.6M shares. I partly discount the strategic equity stakes to reach ~$8/share (10-Q). [citation gate 2026-10-15: estimate, not a reported figure. The 10-Q (July 26, 2026) gives net cash $7,957M = cash 7,037 + short-term investments 2,196 + long-term investments 5,268 less short-term debt 1,299 and long-term debt 5,245, i.e. $10.03/share on 793.6M shares outstanding, or $6.98/share excluding the $2,421M of equity investments; counting half the stakes gives $8.50. ~$8 is a judgment inside that range; see citation_audit.json agent_leg_issues.]
800M diluted in FQ3. Buybacks slowed to $400M in FQ3 and $1.14B over 9M, vs $4.0B a year earlier; $12.8B authorization remains.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM net income $17.0B ($21.5 x 790M) x 72% FCF conversion = $12.2B; at a 3.0% FCF yield = $408B / 790M shares

inputs_detail.input: NTM non-GAAP net income at horizon
inputs_detail.derivation: $21.5 haircut NTM EPS x ~790M diluted shares.

9M FY26 FCF $3.58B / non-GAAP NI $6.98B = 51%; FQ3 alone was $2.33B / $2.80B = 83%. The AR build (DSO 77 vs 72 days, down-payment invoicing and less factoring) should partly reverse, but facilities capex ($1.99B 9M vs $1.48B) stays elevated, so I take a point between the two, below the historical 80-90%.

Semicap trades at 1.2-1.5% FCF yields today, which the skeptic sources call full pricing. On NTM (year-2) cash flow in a late cycle I require 3.0%, the low end of a 3-4% mid-cycle yield. In round 1 I used 2.5% on FY27 FCF; moving the base out a year, I raise the required yield.

bear.story: 2027 proves to be the WFE peak. Micron, TSMC and Samsung signal a 2028 capex pause, the AI-capex pullback theme returns (as in the Sept 14 sell-off), and the BIS Affiliates Rule comes back after the reported Jan 10, 2027 truce deadline, hitting China (28% of revenue, down from 35%) service and parts sales. FY28 EPS is cut to ~$17 (-29% vs the $23.85 consensus), and the multiple de-rates to ~17.5x: 17.5 x 17 + 8 ≈ $305. Precedent: AMAT fell 53% in 2022, and it fell 43% close-to-close from its June 2026 high to the September low with no fundamental shock.

base.story: FY27 is delivered roughly at consensus (~$18.4) and SEMI's +14% 2028 WFE path holds. FY28 expectations settle near $22.5, a little below today's $23.85. The market caps the multiple near 23.5x NTM because it is pricing a late cycle: 23.5 x 22.5 + 8 ≈ $537.

bull.story: The AI fab build keeps accelerating (sell-side 2027 WFE +28-33%, above SEMI's +21.8%). DRAM/HBM capex (Micron FY27 capex stepping up every quarter) and advanced packaging beat, and FY28-29 EPS moves to ~$26. The stock re-rates to ~32x, near its June-high multiple: 32 x 26 + 8 ≈ $840, above the $739.67 intraday high.

thesis_break_reason: $340 is ~18x FY27 consensus ($18.4) and ~14x FY28 consensus ($23.85). That is a downturn multiple on out-year numbers, and it sits 18% below the $415.38 Sept 16 closing low, which came on sentiment alone. A close there would most likely mean a real 2027-28 WFE downturn is being priced: customer capex cuts at the Micron/TSMC/Samsung prints, an AMAT guide-down on Nov 12 or in February, or the Affiliates Rule returning after the reported Jan 10, 2027 deadline alongside broader China restrictions. Ordinary 60%-vol noise would not explain it.

key_uncertainties: Whether the FY28 consensus ($23.85, revenue +20%) survives. It is above SEMI's +14.1% 2028 WFE path, and out-year numbers are what get cut first at a semicap peak.
Late-cycle multiple: ~27.7x FY27 today. The Sep-2027 price depends on whether the multiple on NTM EPS settles near 23x or near 18x.

China (28% of revenue, 35% a year ago) and the BIS Affiliates Rule: the suspension ends Nov 9, 2026 and is reportedly extended to Jan 10, 2027; a suspended BIS denial order also remains from the $252.5M settlement.
Cash conversion: 9M FCF was only 51% of non-GAAP NI (AR build, facilities capex) vs 83% in FQ3. Whether it normalises in FQ4 and FY27.
Structurally low tax rate (non-GAAP ETR 11.0%) that depends on Singapore incentives and global minimum-tax rules. A policy change would cut EPS directly.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor fact-checked three of my round-1 inputs, and I accept each correction. (a) FY28 consensus EPS is $23.85 on $55.5B revenue; I verified this on MarketScreener, which also shows FY27 $18.43. My round-1 $19.5 was 18% below consensus without saying so. (b) SEMI's current (July 2026) path is WFE +21.8% in 2027 and +14.1% in 2028, which does not support near-flat FY28 earnings. (c) My tax-rate and other-income points were wrong as EPS-quality flags: the year-ago 30.6% rate was CAMT-distorted, and the unrealized investment gains are excluded from non-GAAP EPS. I drop both. The valid remainders are the structurally low tax rate, as a policy risk, and FCF conversion, now measured against non-GAAP NI (51% for 9M, 83% for FQ3). I also correct the September closing low ($415.38) and the closing high ($723.00). I verified the Affiliates Rule date independently: the Federal Register suspension ends Nov 9, 2026, and the rule returns Nov 10 unless BIS acts. The Jan 10, 2027 extension comes only from the Steptoe summary, so I carry it as 'reported' and list both dates. Where I keep my own view: I haircut FY28 consensus by 10% rather than the supervisor's 6%. Year-2 consensus revenue growth (+20%) runs ahead of SEMI's +14% 2028 WFE path, and out-year numbers are where semicap cycles break. I also de-rate the multiple to 23.5x NTM. Result: P/E leg $513 and FCF-yield leg $516, blended $514, about spot and up from $505. Scenarios: $305/25%, $537/50%, $840/25% (mean ~$555, median ~$525). Ladder: a mixture of lognormals, 80% with median $540 and sigma 0.42 plus 20% with median $430 and sigma 0.60 to keep a fat left tail for a cycle turn or China shock. That gives P(>=512) = 0.517, up from 0.49, with the tails still consistent with 60% realized vol. The skeptic case remains about the cycle peak and the multiple, not solvency (net cash ~$8/share, investment grade) or accounting. Research in round 2 was limited to 3 searches and 1 fetch.
